items.content: It’s crazy how advanced modern OS schedulers are. When a thread is ready, the scheduler doesn’t just find a free CPU and run it. It has to think about priority, CPU load, affinity, which core the thread ran on before, cache locality, CPU topology, and on heterogeneous systems, which type of core is a better fit. Move the thread too much and you can lose cache locality. Keep it on one busy core and you lose performance. Put background work on a high-performance core and you may waste power. And these decisions happen continuously while hundreds or thousands of threads are waking, sleeping, blocking and competing for CPU time. Scheduling today is as much about power and hardware topology as it is about sharing CPU time.

items.content:
Windows NT 3.1 had an interesting bug where starting an application with "START /REALTIME" could make the OS appear to hang. "/REALTIME" put the process in the real-time priority class, where its threads could run above normal dynamic-priority threads and potentially starve lower-priority work. 

Microsoft documented this as Q103475: “Starting Applications with /REALTIME May Hang Windows NT.” Interestingly, "REALTIME_PRIORITY_CLASS" still exists in Windows today, and Microsoft still warns that misuse can interfere with important system work.

items.content:
RT @justinisgolfing: Even if it is “Noah’s Ark”. All that “proves” is that some dude built a giant boat. Nothing more and nothing less. 

A “global flood” covering “all the high hills under the whole heaven” as stated in Genesis 7 did not happen… and the evidence is not subtle.

1. Earth does not have enough water to drown Everest. All ice, groundwater, and atmospheric moisture together still leave the high ranges far above any plausible flood surface. 

2. A year-long global flood would also leave one chaotic, same-age layer of mixed marine and land fossils on every continent. That layer does not exist.

3. Greenland and Antarctic ice cores, lake varves, and tree-ring sequences show continuous annual layers going back tens to hundreds of thousands of years with no flood interruption. 

4. Footprints, burrows, and standing trees occur throughout rocks, that flood-geology assigns to the possible years of the Flood. 

5. Egypt, Mesopotamia, and China kept going through the dates ranges assigned to Noah. No global reset. ￼

6. Flood myths are common because river valleys flood. The Ark story as a worldwide, mountain-covering catastrophe is factually impossibke based on factual (not theoretical) evidence.

any process can read and write it.

24 seconds. no consent sheet.
Lockdown Mode does not save you if the hub was already trusted.

items.content:
RT @MsftSecIntel: Across intrusions leading to different ransomware payloads, the ransomware affiliate Storm-2570 has used consistent post-compromise tools and techniques, highlighting the value of monitoring recurring attacker behaviors rather than tracking payloads alone. https://t.co/h41vwrFs1Z

Storm-2570 has used largely uniform tradecraft, including remote access, credential theft, lateral movement, security tampering, and data exfiltration, across deployments involving Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis, and BERT ransomware.

Read the latest Microsoft Threat Intelligence blog for a comprehensive analysis of Storm-2570 activity, as well as Microsoft Defender detections, hunting guidance, and relevant mitigation recommendations, including tamper protection, credential hygiene, and configuring automatic attack disruption.
